transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
Ukrainian drones lost some of their speed after restrictions were suddenly imposed on
battlefield use of the country's Starlink communication terminals, which are operated
by SpaceX.
It comes after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the Trump administration threatened
to stop sharing intelligence with Ukraine, as NPR's Greg Myry explains.
NPR's Ukraine correspondent Joanna Kekissis interviewed President Zelensky in Kyiv.
This was just hours before this latest development we're talking about, and she asked Zelensky
if the U.S. was going to cut off intelligence.
Here's what he said.
We need Starlink.
We asked administration, government, and SpaceX on different channels.
We asked them to share with us Starlink, only for military goals.
So, Trump said yesterday that intelligence sharing hadn't been cut off, but what we're
seeing today certainly looks like an intentional action to limit Ukraine's ability to fight
Russia.
NPR's Greg Myry reporting.
With 20 days until the midterm elections, President Trump is concentrating on Republican-leaning
states.
He stopped in Arizona today and is on his way to Montana, and NPR's Stephen Fowler says
next week Trump heads to Kansas, which has become a newly competitive state.
Kansas is a state with an outgoing Democratic governor and a Republican U.S. Senator on the
ballot, but polls show voters could pick a Republican to retake the governor's office
and send a Democrat to the Senate for the first time in nearly a century.
On the one hand, the president's deeply unpopular economic policies have hit states
like Kansas hard.
On the other, Republicans have been appealing to voters with local solutions to issues like
affordability and lower energy prices in their bid for the governor's seat, which leads
to Trump spending one of the final days of the midterms in Wichita, campaigning in a
state he won by more than 16 points in 2024.
Stephen Fowler, NPR News, Dodge City, Kansas.
A new survey finds more than four in 10 Americans had difficulty paying for at least one basic
necessity in the past year.
NPR's Jennifer Ludden reports it comes as the cost of living is a top election issue
for voters.
Paying for medical care was the biggest challenge people faced, including for more than a quarter
of middle-income households.
Just according to a survey by the Pew Research Center, next was daily transportation, housing
and food.
Nearly a third who struggled to pay for these things said they'd taken it alone.
Even more borrowed money from friends and family.
Pew also finds more than half of Americans did not have enough emergency savings to cover
expenses for three months.
The findings come amid stubborn inflation, with prices climbing faster than most people's
paychecks driven in part by the war with Iran.
Jennifer Ludden, NPR News, Washington.
And U.S. inflation accelerated last month as gas, clothes and airfare got more expensive.
The consumer price index rose 3.7 percent in September, compared with a year ago, up
from 3.4 percent in August.
This is NPR News.
A Texas prosecutor says an ICE officer appeared to intentionally drive into a man in Houston
breaking his leg.
Harris County Democratic District Attorney Sean Tier says he's considering criminal charges
against the driver.
The encounter has sent off new protests in Houston where an ICE officer fatally shot
a man this summer.
Scientists have discovered that elephants have an outsized impact on landscapes, not
just in life, but also in death.
Alana Gordon reports.
Elephants are ecosystem engineers.
They knock down trees, they disperse seeds, but scientists in South Africa's Kruger National
Park found something they didn't expect after the animals die.
The group monitored dozens of elephant carcasses on the savannah, and found that over time,
their remains created unique, nutrient-rich hot spots for certain grasses.
This drew animals like zebras and antelope well after any visual signs of the elephant
had disappeared.
Courtney Reed is with UC Santa Barbara in Princeton.
She led the research.
Seeing that even like eight years on, you have all of these different herbivores that
live on the savannah that are really selecting for those nitrogen-rich grasses.
It was just exciting.
Reed says this lasting legacy highlights the importance of elephants as they face threats
of extinction.
The findings were published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
Alana Gordon, NPR News.
A small dog named Luna has been found after a month on the loose in Yellowstone National
Park.
Though spotted frequently, the Jack Russell Terrier evaded capture since early September.
Volunteers were able to catch the dog today using a live trap baited with her owner's
scent using a t-shirt and pillowcase belonging to the family.
I'm Rylan Barton, and from Washington, this is NPR News.
[BLANK_AUDIO]

topics.text: Ukrainian drones slowed after sudden limits on SpaceX Starlink terminal use in combat
Zelensky says Trump administration threatened to halt U.S. intelligence sharing with Ukraine
Trump campaigns in Arizona and Montana, with Kansas stop planned for Wichita
Pew survey finds over 40% of Americans struggled to pay for a basic necessity
U.S. consumer prices rose 3.7% year over year in September, up from August
Texas prosecutor considers charges against ICE officer who allegedly drove into man in Houston
Kruger National Park study finds dead elephants create lasting nutrient-rich grassland hotspots
Jack Russell Terrier named Luna recaptured in Yellowstone after month-long search
